judge.delivered_result: A spectral evolution in which the dialkylphosphorochloridate intermediate shows one signal (~0 to +10 ppm), POCl3 appears at +35 to +48 ppm, and the final dialkyl phosphate gives one peak or 'two closely spaced singlets' (0 to –5 ppm), with a 'possible doublet for diastereomers'.
judge.correct_result: Over the course of the final hydrolysis, both the starting phosphorochloridate RO–P(O)(Cl)(OR') and the product RO–P(O)(OR')(OH) are chiral at phosphorus; with two different enantiopure alcohols each is formed as two diastereomers, so the proton-decoupled 31P NMR shows two starting chloridate singlets decreasing and two new phosphate singlets growing (two pairs of peaks during the reaction, ending with two peaks for the product).
